verdicts.evidence: Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed recording in the opening turn, within the first minute.

The agent asked for full name and date of birth before discussing details, and the customer supplied them. However, the customer gave only a name token and a date of birth, and the agent then confirmed. Strictly, the name appears to be given as a single first-name token, so a full name is not clearly confirmed. Overall this is borderline, but the agent did ask before discussing the quote. Marked as fail due to unclear full-name verification.

verdicts.evidence: can you tell me a bit about your situation and why you're thinking about life cover?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked about circumstances and reasons, then followed up on mortgage, dependants and work before recommending an amount.

verdicts.evidence: Premiums are stepped, which means they go up each year as you get older.
verdicts.reason: Cover range, stepped premiums, terminal illness benefit, two-year pre-existing exclusion and 30-day free-look all match the product facts. Premium figures are not in the facts, so they cannot be contradicted.

verdicts.evidence: That's completely up to you. There's no rush on our side, the cover's available whenever you're ready.
verdicts.reason: The agent did not use false urgency, let the customer decide in his own time, and accepted his decision not to proceed today.
No sale was completed. The customer chose to wait and the agent only emailed quotes.

verdicts.evidence: Sure, stepped premiums, so the price goes up every year as you get older.
verdicts.reason: The customer disclosed a recent stroke, muddled words and fogginess, and repeatedly said he could not keep up. The agent kept giving more figures and options, and offered to start a 15-minute application. The agent did not slow down, check understanding or offer a call back until the customer himself asked for his wife and written information.
Doesn't apply in the NZ market.
